# Story 1.1: Enrol an authenticator app
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder, I want to enrol an authenticator app by scanning a QR code, so that I can protect my sign-in with time-based codes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a signed-in user with 2FA off, when they start enrolment, then the page shows a QR code their authenticator app can scan.
- AC-2: Given the user has scanned the QR code, when they submit the code their app currently generates, then enrolment completes and their account shows 2FA as enabled.
- AC-3: Given the user has scanned the QR code, when they submit a code that does not match, then enrolment does not complete, 2FA stays off, and the page shows an error asking for a new code.
- AC-4: Given the user leaves enrolment before confirming a code, when they next view their account, then 2FA is still off.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Add `totp_secret` column to the users table and store the pending secret when enrolment starts (AC: 1, 4)
- [ ] Render the authenticator provisioning URI as a QR code on the enrolment page (AC: 1)
- [ ] Verify the submitted code against the pending secret with pyotp; on a match, mark 2FA enabled (AC: 2, 3)
- [ ] On a mismatch, show the error and leave 2FA disabled (AC: 3, 4)

## Dev Notes
- FR-1 is the requirement behind this story: enrolment is only complete after the user confirms one generated code.
- The architecture adds `totp_secret` to the users table and verifies TOTP with pyotp in the existing Flask app, with no new service.

Status: ready-for-dev

As an account holder with 2FA enabled, I want sign-in to ask for a authenticator code after my password, so that a stolen password alone cannot sign me in.

- AC-2: Given the code prompt, when they submit the current valid TOTP code, then they are signed in.
- AC-3: Given the code prompt, when they submit an invalid or expired code, then they are not signed in and see an error.
- AC-4: Given a user with 2FA off, when they submit the correct password, then they are signed in with no code prompt.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] After a correct password, hold the login as pending when 2FA is enabled and sign in directly when it is not (AC: 1, 4)
- [ ] Verify the submitted code against the user's `totp_secret` with pyotp and complete sign-in only on a match (AC: 2, 3)
- [ ] Show the code prompt and the invalid-code error in the login flow (AC: 1, 3)

## Dev Notes
- FR-2 is the requirement behind this story: sign-in requires a valid TOTP code after the password step.
- The architecture verifies TOTP with pyotp in the existing Flask app, and the pending state is held in the existing session-cookie login.

- [ ] Generate ten distinct recovery codes when enrolment is confirmed, and store them on the account (AC: 1, 2)

- [ ] Issue codes only on the confirmation path, never while enrolment is pending (AC: 3)

# Story 1.4: Sign in with a recovery code
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder who has lost my authenticator device, I want to use one of my recovery codes in place of a TOTP code, so that I can regain access to my account.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given 2FA is enabled and I am at the code step, when I submit one of my unused recovery codes, then I am signed in.
- AC-2: Given I have already used a recovery code, when I submit that same code again, then I am not signed in and I see an error.
- AC-3: Given I am at the code step, when I submit a recovery code that belongs to another account, then I am not signed in.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Accept a recovery code at the code step as an alternative to a TOTP code (AC: 1, 3)
- [ ] Mark a recovery code as used on its first successful sign-in (AC: 1, 2)
- [ ] Reject a recovery code that has already been used, with an error (AC: 2)
- [ ] Match recovery codes only against the signing-in account's stored codes (AC: 3)

## Dev Notes
- FR-3 is the requirement behind this story. Any one of the ten codes replaces a TOTP code once, so each use must consume the code.
- Architecture: recovery codes are read from the `recovery_codes` column. TOTP verification with pyotp covers only TOTP codes, so recovery codes are checked against the stored set in the same Flask app with no new service.

- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-3]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#data-model]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#verification]

- Nothing covers regenerating codes, disabling 2FA, or what happens when all ten are used.
- Nothing covers rate-limiting failed code attempts.
- The architecture does not name a QR-rendering library.

I used epic `1` and split FR-3 into two stories (issuance and redemption) because a user notices those separately.

Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As a workspace owner, I want to request a CSV export of all my workspace's members, so that I can take the member list out of the app.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given I am a workspace owner, when I request a CSV export, then the request is accepted and I see a message that the export is being prepared.

- [ ] Refuse the request for non-owners before any export is enqueued (AC: 2)

## Dev Notes

# Story 1.2: Owner is emailed a download link when the export is ready
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As a workspace owner, I want to be emailed a download link when my export is ready, so that I can get the file without waiting on the page.

- AC-1: Given I have requested an export, when the file has been prepared, then I receive an email containing a download link.

- AC-3: Given I have received the email, when I open the download link, then I download the CSV file of workspace members.

- [ ] Have the request dispatch the task and return immediately (AC: 2)

- [ ] Send the owner the download-link email through SES once the file is written (AC: 1)

- FR-2 is the requirement behind this story. The architecture runs exports as a Celery task, writes them to S3 under a per-workspace prefix, serves them through a presigned URL, and sends mail through SES. The link's lifetime is set in Story 1.4.

# Story 1.3: Rate-limit counters survive an application restart
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an API operator, I want rate-limit counters to persist across restarts, so that restarting the service does not hand every client a fresh budget.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a client has used part of its limit in the current window, when the application restarts within that window, then the client's remaining budget is what it was before the restart.
- AC-2: Given a client has reached its limit in the current window, when the application restarts within that window and the client sends another request, then the response is 429.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Hold per-key counters in Redis rather than in application memory (AC: 1, 2)
- [ ] Give each counter a time-to-live of one limit window so it clears on its own when the window ends (AC: 1, 2)
- [ ] Test that a restart mid-window preserves the count and the 429 (AC: 1, 2)

## Dev Notes
- CAP-1 is the requirement behind this story. Constraint: Redis is already in the stack as the intended counter store, so counters held there are not lost when the application process restarts.
